group.passage: Solar panels are now a common sight on rooftops and in open fields. Few people realize, however, that the story of turning sunlight into electricity began almost two hundred years ago, long before anyone had a use for it. The first step came in 1839, when the French scientist Edmond Becquerel noticed that light could increase the electricity produced in one of his experiments. In 1883, an American inventor named Charles Fritts made the first solar cells from a material called selenium. His cells worked, but they turned only a very small part of the sunlight into power, so they were not able to run real machines. The real breakthrough happened in 1954 at Bell Labs in the United States. Three scientists there, Daryl Chapin, Calvin Fuller, and Gerald Pearson, made a solar cell out of silicon, and it was the first one strong enough to run everyday electrical equipment. Their first version changed about 4 percent of the sunlight into electricity, and later versions reached 11 percent. At first, the new cells did not sell well, but they soon found an important job in space. In 1958, a satellite called Vanguard I carried a small set of them to power its radios. A few years later, in 1963, Japan put a 242-watt solar system on a lighthouse, the largest of its kind at that time. For many years after that, solar power remained a very small part of the world's electricity. The chart below shows how quickly this has changed in recent years. In 2010, solar power produced only 0.2 percent of the world's electricity. By 2020, the share had grown to 3.2 percent, and by 2025 it had reached 8.7 percent. Because solar power does not burn coal or gas, its fast growth is good news for people who want cleaner air and a cooler planet.

questions.stem: What does “them” in the third paragraph refer to?
According to the chart, about what share of the world's electricity came from solar power in 2015?

1.explanation_zh: 第一段說把陽光變成電的故事從將近兩百年前就開始了；第二、三段依時間介紹 1839、1883、1954、1958、1963 年的發展；第四段用圖表說明近年太陽能占全球電力的比例快速上升。全文講的是太陽能發電一路以來的成長。
evidence: Few people realize, however, that the story of turning sunlight into electricity began almost two hundred years ago, long before anyone had a use for it.
The chart below shows how quickly this has changed in recent years.

option_notes_zh.A: 衛星和無線電只在第三段出現，而且文中說的是太陽能電池替無線電供電。
option_notes_zh.B: 文中沒有教人怎麼在屋頂裝太陽能板。
option_notes_zh.C: Becquerel 只出現在第二段第一句，文中沒有介紹他的一生。

1.strategy_zh: 主旨題要涵蓋「早期的發現」和「近年的成長」兩部分，只講其中一個人或一件事的選項都太窄。
hints: 第一段第二句說「把陽光變成電的故事」從什麼時候開始？
第二、三段是依時間排列的發展；第四段的圖表顯示什麼的變化？
選能同時涵蓋早期歷史與近年成長的選項。

2.explanation_zh: 第三段說 1954 年 Bell Labs 用矽做的太陽能電池，是第一個強到能讓日常電器運轉的電池。
evidence: Three scientists there, Daryl Chapin, Calvin Fuller, and Gerald Pearson, made a solar cell out of silicon, and it was the first one strong enough to run everyday electrical equipment.

option_notes_zh.B: selenium（硒）是 1883 年 Fritts 用的材料；Bell Labs 用的是 silicon（矽）。
option_notes_zh.C: 裝在燈塔上的是 1963 年日本的太陽能系統。
option_notes_zh.D: 第一版只把大約 4% 的陽光變成電，後來也只到 11%。

2.strategy_zh: 用 Bell Labs、1954 定位到第三段第一、二句，把每個選項和原句比對。
hints: 找第三段的 1954 和 Bell Labs。
下一句說這個矽電池是第一個能做到什麼的電池？
run everyday electrical equipment 換個說法是什麼？

3.explanation_zh: 前一句說「這些新的電池」起初賣得不好，但很快在太空中找到重要的工作；接著說 1958 年 Vanguard I 衛星載了一小組 them 來替無線電供電，所以 them 指太陽能電池。
evidence: At first, the new cells did not sell well, but they soon found an important job in space.
In 1958, a satellite called Vanguard I carried a small set of them to power its radios.

option_notes_zh.A: radios 是被供電的對象，「用無線電來替無線電供電」說不通。
option_notes_zh.B: 科學家出現在更前面的句子，不會被「一小組」裝上衛星替無線電供電。
option_notes_zh.D: 句中只有一顆衛星 Vanguard I，而且它是載運的主體。

3.strategy_zh: 代名詞題先看前一句的主詞，再把候選詞代回原句，看意思通不通。
hints: them 是複數，前一句的主詞是什麼複數名詞？
把 the new cells 代回：carried a small set of the new cells to power its radios。
其他選項代回去，意思通嗎？

4.strategy_zh: 讀圖題先在橫軸找到題目問的年份，再讀那一點對應的數值；注意文中沒寫的年份一定要看圖。
hints: 對照縱軸或資料表，2015 年那一點是多少？
其他三個數字分別是哪一年的？

translation_zh.text:
太陽能板現在在屋頂和空曠的田野上很常見。不過，很少人知道，把陽光變成電的故事在將近兩百年前就開始了，遠在任何人用得上它之前。
第一步出現在 1839 年，法國科學家埃德蒙・貝克勒爾發現，光能讓他某個實驗產生的電變多。1883 年，一位名叫查爾斯・弗里茨的美國發明家，用一種叫做硒的材料做出第一批太陽能電池。他的電池能運作，但只能把非常少的陽光變成電力，所以無法讓真正的機器運轉。
真正的突破發生在 1954 年美國的貝爾實驗室。那裡的三位科學家——達里爾・查平、卡爾文・富勒和傑拉德・皮爾森——用矽做出一種太陽能電池，它是第一個強到能讓日常電器運轉的電池。他們的第一版大約能把 4% 的陽光變成電，後來的版本達到 11%。起初，這種新電池賣得不好，但它們很快就在太空中找到了重要的工作。1958 年，一顆名叫先鋒一號的衛星載了一小組這種電池，替它的無線電供電。幾年後的 1963 年，日本在一座燈塔上裝了一套 242 瓦的太陽能系統，是當時同類中最大的。
在那之後的許多年裡，太陽能在全世界的電力中仍只占很小的一部分。下面的圖表顯示，近年來這種情況改變得有多快。2010 年，太陽能只產生全世界 0.2% 的電力。到了 2020 年，這個比例增加到 3.2%，到 2025 年則達到 8.7%。因為太陽能發電不必燃燒煤或天然氣，它的快速成長，對希望空氣更乾淨、地球更涼爽的人來說是好消息。

evidence: Few people realize, however, that the story of turning sunlight into electricity began almost two hundred years ago, long before anyone had a use for it.

A.evidence: In 1958, a satellite called Vanguard I carried a small set of them to power its radios.

In 1839 the French scientist Edmond Becquerel noticed that light could increase the electricity produced in one of his experiments.（f1；DOE 年表 PDF 2026-10-09 複查一致）
In 1883 the American inventor Charles Fritts made the first solar cells from selenium; they could not run real machines.（f2、f3；DOE 年表一致）
In 1954 at Bell Labs, Daryl Chapin, Calvin Fuller, and Gerald Pearson made a silicon solar cell, the first strong enough to run everyday electrical equipment.（f4；DOE 年表一致）
Their first version changed about 4 percent of the sunlight into electricity, and later versions reached 11 percent.（f5；DOE 年表：4% efficiency、later achieved 11%）
